extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, Medicare billing/coding staff, hospital finance officers, transplant centers, medical device manufacturers, and stakeholders preparing comments on the FY 2027 IPPS proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Federal CMS proposed-rule guidance for calculating FY 2027 MS-DRG cost-based relative weights, national cost-to-charge ratios, data inclusion/exclusion rules, handling of special-case DRGs (notably MS-DRG 018 CAR T-cell/immunotherapy), and criteria/process for new technology add-on payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim type inclusion/exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Include only inpatient claims paid as fee-for-service (claim type "60"); exclude claims with claim type values not equal to "60" (claim types "61","62","63","64" relate to encounter, MA IME, HMO no-pay and are excluded). Also exclude CAHs and Rural Emergency Hospitals (REHs), including hospitals that became CAHs/REHs after the data period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This determines the universe of MedPAR claims used to calculate relative weights for FY 2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouper and coding version for weighting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes and ICD-10-PCS procedure codes from the FY 2025 MedPAR claims data, grouped through the ICD-10 version of the proposed FY 2027 GROUPER (Version 44).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All claims are regrouped using the proposed FY 2027 MS-DRG classifications where possible (see sections II.B/II.C of preamble).

rubrics_metrics.name: HCRIS dataset vintage for CCRs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Medicare cost report data files from the Healthcare Cost Report Information System (HCRIS) that are three years prior to the IPPS fiscal year; specifically, the December 2025 update of the FY 2024 HCRIS is used for FY 2027 CCRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS posts the HCRIS version used and the derived national average CCRs on its website for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transplant-case inclusion limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Transplant cases used to establish relative weights for specified transplant MS-DRGs were limited to Medicare-approved transplant centers that have cases in the FY 2025 MedPAR file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medicare transplants (heart, heart-lung, liver/intestinal, lung) are limited to facilities approved by CMS as transplant centers; only their cases in the historical file are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtract organ acquisition charges from transplant bills
rubrics_metrics.description: Organ acquisition costs (kidney, heart, heart-lung, liver, lung, pancreas, intestinal/multivisceral) are paid separately on a reasonable cost basis and must be subtracted from total charges on transplant bills that show acquisition charges before computing average cost and eliminating outliers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents organ acquisition charges (paid outside the prospective payment rate) from inflating MS-DRG cost measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtract hematopoietic stem cell acquisition charges
rubrics_metrics.description: For cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2020, costs related to hematopoietic stem cell acquisition for allogeneic HSCT are paid on a reasonable cost basis; hematopoietic stem cell acquisition charges are subtracted from total charges on transplant bills that show such charges before computing average cost and eliminating outliers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies for FY 2022 and subsequent years; see FY 2021 final rule discussion for historical context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delete claims with non-positive charges or LOS or charge-field inconsistencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims with total charges or total lengths of stay less than or equal to zero are deleted. Claims where the total charge field differs by more than $30.00 from the sum of detailed charge components are deleted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a data quality filter to remove implausible or internally inconsistent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider cost-center completeness requirement (14 of 19 rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: At least 92.5 percent of providers in the MedPAR file had charges for 14 of the 19 cost centers. Claims for providers that did not have charges greater than zero for at least 14 of the 19 cost centers were deleted (a provider may have no more than five blank cost centers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures sufficient departmental charge reporting per provider for CCR derivation and weighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical outlier elimination (3.0 SD on log distribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove all cases beyond 3.0 standard deviations from the geometric mean of the log distribution of both total charges per case and total charges per day for each MS-DRG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outliers are removed after standardization and before conversion to costs to avoid skewing MS-DRG average costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: POA indicator reset to 'Y' for relative weight-setting
rubrics_metrics.description: For relative weight-setting purposes only, reset Present on Admission (POA) indicators that are 'N' (No) or 'U' (unknown/insufficient documentation) to 'Y' (Yes) to avoid misclassification of HACs inflating relative weights of lower-severity MS-DRGs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 'forced' reassignment places costly HAC cases into higher severity MS-DRGs so relative weights better reflect true costs and preserves budget-neutrality integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize charges to remove geographic/wage/IME/DSH/COLA effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges for each of the 19 cost groups for each claim are standardized to remove effects of differences in area wage levels, IME and DSH payments, and for Alaska/Hawaii applicable cost-of-living adjustments; also remove geographic adjustment factors and DSH payments under capital IPPS when standardizing total charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardization is applied prior to summing charges by MS-DRG and before applying CCRs to convert to costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 19 cost centers and supplemental mapping file
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS used 19 cost centers (defined and shown in a supplemental Cost Center HCRIS Lines Supplemental Data File) to create national cost-center CCRs by mapping cost report lines to revenue codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supplemental file lists cost report lines and corresponding revenue codes used; CMS may consider comments about these groupings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply national average CCRs to convert standardized charges to costs
rubrics_metrics.description: After summing standardized charges by MS-DRG across the 19 cost centers, charges are converted to costs by applying the proposed national average CCRs developed from the FY 2024 cost report data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The national average CCRs are charge-weighted and posted on the CMS website; after conversion, total standardized costs per MS-DRG are computed for average cost calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-monotonicity handling by combining severity levels
rubrics_metrics.description: If mean cost in a higher severity level is less than mean cost in the lower level (non-monotonic), combine cases that group to the specific non-monotonic MS-DRGs for relative weight calculations so the resulting relative weights are monotonic (equalized across combined DRGs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS applies this procedure to identified MS-DRG pairs (e.g., 217/218, 504/505, 582/584) and reports statistics both separately and with cases combined in supplemental files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization of recalibrated relative weights
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed FY 2027 cost-based relative weights were normalized by an adjustment factor (1.944557) so that the average case weight after recalibration equals the average case weight before recalibration, preserving budget neutrality under section 1886(d)(4)(C)(iii) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalization assures recalibration alone neither increases nor decreases total IPPS payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cap on relative weight reductions (permanent 10% cap)
rubrics_metrics.description: A permanent 10-percent cap on the reduction in an MS-DRG's relative weight in a given fiscal year is applied (effective beginning FY 2023). For MS-DRGs that would otherwise decline by more than 10% from the prior year, set the new relative weight equal to 90% of the prior year weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS applies a budget-neutrality adjustment to the standardized amount so the permanent cap does not change estimated aggregate payments; supplemental files demonstrate cap application for FY 2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development and trimming rules for national average CCRs
rubrics_metrics.description: Using FY 2024 cost reports, CMS removed CAHs, REHs, Indian Health Service hospitals, all-inclusive rate hospitals, and cost reports representing periods <365 days. CCRs greater than 10 or less than 0.01 were removed. Departmental CCRs were normalized by dividing each department CCR by the hospital total CCR. Logs of normalized CCRs were trimmed beyond mean log ±3 standard deviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After trimming, create Medicare-specific CCRs by applying hospital departmental CCRs to Medicare charges (Worksheet D-3), sum Medicare-specific costs and charges, and derive national average charge-weighted CCRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum case threshold and low-volume MS-DRG treatment (10-case rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Historically and proposed for FY 2027, a threshold of 10 cases is used as the minimum number of cases to compute a reasonable weight. For MS-DRGs with fewer than 10 cases, compute relative weights by adjusting their final FY 2026 relative weights by the percentage change in the average weight of the cases in other MS-DRGs from FY 2026 to FY 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach addresses instability in weight estimates for very low-volume MS-DRGs.

rubrics_metrics.name: MS-DRG 018: identification and exclusion of clinical trial/expanded access/immunotherapy-not-purchased cases
rubrics_metrics.description: When calculating the average cost for MS-DRG 018 (CAR T-cell/immunotherapy), exclude claims that (1) contain ICD-10-CM diagnosis code Z00.6 and do not include payer-only code 'ZC', (2) contain condition code '90' (or for earlier years 'ZB'), or (3) contain standardized drug charges below the median standardized drug charge of clinical trial cases in MS-DRG 018 (proposed temporary proxy for cases where product is not purchased in the usual manner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS no longer uses the proxy of standardized drug charges <$373,000; instead it excludes based on codes Z00.6 without ZC, condition code 90, or the median-trim rule for FYs 2026–2027 until data include a direct condition code for products not purchased in the usual manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: MS-DRG 018 adjustor calculation and application
rubrics_metrics.description: To calculate an adjustor for clinical trial/expanded access/immunotherapy-not-purchased cases in MS-DRG 018: (1) calculate average cost for cases identified as clinical trial/expanded access/etc.; (2) calculate average cost for all other MS-DRG 018 cases; (3) divide (1) by (2) to obtain an adjustor; (4) apply the adjustor to the identified cases and add the adjusted case count to non-clinical trial case count prior to calculating the national average cost per case and for budget neutrality/outlier simulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS estimated an adjustor of 0.17 for the FY 2027 proposed rule based on December 2025 data (clinical trial avg cost $71,039 vs non-clinical trial $412,218) and proposes updating the adjustor for the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cap application and budget-neutrality adjustment visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the permanent 10% cap on relative weight reductions after normalization; provide supplemental files (Addendum and CMS website) showing the budget-neutrality adjustment associated with reclassification and recalibration with cap application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS posts supplemental demonstrations and data files for transparency and invites comments on recalibration and weight changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: New technology add-on payment criteria (three statutory/regulatory elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 42 CFR 412.87, an applicant for a new medical service or technology add-on payment must satisfy three criteria: (1) the service or technology must be new; (2) it must be costly such that the applicable MS-DRG prospective payment rate is inadequate (cost criterion); and (3) it must demonstrate a substantial clinical improvement over existing services/technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain transformative devices and antimicrobials may qualify under alternative pathways (§412.87(c),(d)). Capital costs are not included in add-on payments (capital costs covered separately under §1886(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Newness / substantial similarity test for new technology add-on
rubrics_metrics.description: A service/technology is not 'new' if substantially similar to existing technologies. The FY 2010 criteria for substantial similarity consider: (1) whether the product uses the same or a similar mechanism of action to achieve a therapeutic outcome; (2) whether the product is assigned to the same or a different MS-DRG; and (3) whether the new use involves treatment of the same or similar disease and patient population. If all three are met, the product is substantially similar and not 'new.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even newly FDA-authorized products may not qualify if substantially similar to older marketed products (often assessed over a 2–3 year market window).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost criterion evaluation and threshold methodology for add-on eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To assess adequacy of payment for new technology, evaluate whether charges of cases involving the technology exceed a threshold equal to the lesser of: (a) 75 percent of the standardized amount (increased to reflect difference between cost and charges), or (b) 75 percent of one standard deviation beyond the geometric mean standardized charge for all cases in the MS-DRG (or case-weighted average across relevant MS-DRGs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS publishes the MS-DRG threshold amounts in data files associated with the IPPS rules; beginning FY 2022 CMS uses proposed threshold values from the proposed rule to evaluate applications for that fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant data submission guidance (sample size and HIPAA considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should submit a significant sample of data to demonstrate that the service/technology meets the high-cost threshold; sample size should enable CMS to undertake validation and analysis. CMS has discussed applicability of the HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR part 160 and part 164 subparts A and E) to claims information submitted with add-on applications and provided prior guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to prior IPPS final rules (e.g., FY 2012) for more detailed discussion; applicants should consider data sufficiency and privacy regulation implications when submitting claims data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of capital costs from new technology add-on payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Add-on payments for new medical services/technologies under IPPS do not include capital costs; capital costs are covered under the capital IPPS (section 1886(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction was reiterated from prior rulemaking (e.g., 72 FR 47307–47308).
